clue.text: Confesses personal matter, upon reflection

parts.note: personal means one's own

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word for matter is read backwards

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a private matter after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personal matter' reads as one phrase but splits in two; 'upon reflection' reverses only the second word's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom for admitting guilt, which is what someone who confesses does.

clue.text: How flawless execution proceeds, despite all one's efforts?

definitions.meaning: an executor carries out a will; the job goes perfectly ..., a testament to beat all others
the idiom ... means however hard one tries

explanation.surface: A wry question about how a perfect performance fares despite trying hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' means carrying out a will, so the first reading is literal: the finest will there is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said when good intentions cannot achieve something, so it means despite every effort.

clue.text: Wise man's got millions, working unaided to begin with

indicators.note: the word for unaided is put at the start, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: solo means alone, unaided
M stands for million(s)
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A wise man made his fortune by first going it alone.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for wisdom, so a Solomon is a wise man.

clue.text: Pharisee admitting ignoble end for gentile is right

indicators.note: letting in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a Pharisee is a self-righteous person, a prig
vile means base, ignoble

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A Pharisee conceding a base fate for a non-Jew is justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pharisee' suggests the Bible, but here it is the general sense of a sanctimonious, self-righteous person; 'admitting' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or advantage granted to someone.

clue.text: Rushing wind postponed start of mission

parts.note: a blast is a sudden rush of wind
an event called off, or simply off, has been postponed or cancelled

explanation.surface: A gale forces a mission's start to be delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast-off is the launch of a rocket, the moment a space mission begins.

clue.text: Valiant attempt to repress one's initial prejudice

indicators.note: holding something down inside, so the two words enclose the letter

parts.note: a big effort or gesture can be a valiant one
a try is an attempt

indicators.note: the first letter of the word one's is taken

explanation.surface: A brave effort to suppress one's first prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repress' signals that the attempt holds the letter within it; the 's of one's belongs to the word whose initial is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerant prejudice against people of other views or groups.

clue.text: Several seaweeds good in salad uncovered close to shore

indicators.note: the letter for good is placed inside the trimmed word
with its covering, the outer letters, stripped off
the close, or final letter, of the following word

explanation.surface: Seaweed gathered near the shore turns up in a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips SALAD to ALA; G goes in, then E from 'shore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Algae is a plural, and many seaweeds are types of algae.

clue.text: One particular doctor choking to death

indicators.note: the two pieces close around the word to, gripping it between them

parts.note: the definite article the picks out one particular thing
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A certain doctor is choking someone to death.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomb stands for death by metonymy, as in going to the tomb, the grave.

clue.text: What could make any fellow claim a discontinued benefit?

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to make the answer, so these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A question about what would let any man claim an abolished welfare payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Family allowance was the UK weekly payment to parents, replaced by child benefit in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: Family allowance was a British state payment for children that no longer exists, a benefit discontinued.

clue.text: Prevarication unlikely in serenade

indicators.note: one word placed in another: the word for unlikely goes inside the word for serenade

parts.note: to serenade someone is to sing to them
a tall story is an unlikely one

explanation.surface: A doubtful excuse is slipped into a love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' works through the idiom a tall story, an unlikely tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalling is playing for time with evasions, which is a form of prevarication.

clue.text: On German lake, last of the morning sun shimmers

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: S is short for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: Sunlight dances on a German lake late in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleams and shimmers are both verbs for light glinting or flickering on a surface.

clue.text: One thing or a couple?

definitions.meaning: a single thing in a list or collection
two people in a relationship are said to be an ...

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether something is single or a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Item has both senses: an individual article and, informally, a romantically linked pair.

clue.text: See 2
Bloke that is limiting expense, essentially

definitions.text: Bloke that is limiting expense, essentially

indicators.note: the outer letters enclose the inner one, holding it in

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stingy man who keeps spending down to the essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'expense' is E, which goes inside MANIE after the M. As a whole the clue describes a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a stingy, ungenerous person, exactly a man who keeps his spending down.

clue.text: Animated character's loud warning cry turned attention

indicators.note: turned round, so the two words for loud and warning cry are read backwards together

parts.note: a big noise is a loud one
oy is a shout to get someone's attention or warn them
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A cartoon character yells a warning and gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes BIGOY into YOGIB; EAR then follows. The 's is a link (character is).
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is a Hanna-Barbera cartoon bear from Jellystone Park.

clue.text: Pressman backing into barn with small cultivators

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the word for barn

parts.note: a garner is a granary or barn

indicators.note: going backwards, so the editor's abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: an editor, ED, is a man of the press

explanation.surface: A journalist reverses into a barn full of farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the editor; 'into' puts the result inside the old word garner, a granary.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners are people who cultivate plants, so they are cultivators.

clue.text: Tiniest particle in balance

indicators.note: the word for particle sits within the word for balance

parts.note: the rest is the balance, what remains
a mote is a speck of dust

explanation.surface: A minute speck sits in a set of scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' looks like scales but means the remainder, REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Remotest is used for the smallest possible degree, as in not the remotest chance.

clue.text: Finished drink, partly a coincidence

parts.note: over means finished
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Finishing a drink together turns out to be partly chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is a partial coincidence, where two things share some ground or time but not all.

clue.text: Devise fine trophy for orators

indicators.note: speakers would say it, so the phrase is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: fine means thin, as a fine thread; a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: Come up with a good prize for public speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To think up a plan is to invent or devise it.

clue.text: Disorder created by politician in government

indicators.note: the politician is placed in the word for government

parts.note: rule is government of a country
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician in office causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple is to make untidy or crumple, so to disorder hair or clothes.

clue.text: Attentive guard taken short

parts.note: to mind something is to look after or guard it

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: seats that are taken are full, all occupied

explanation.surface: A sentry caught out needing the toilet stays alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken short' is an idiom for urgently needing the toilet, a misleading surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindful means aware or heedful, so attentive to something.

clue.text: Rationalise current business

parts.note: a stream is a flowing current of water
one's line is one's business or trade

explanation.surface: A company is urged to modernise its present operations.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline an organisation is to make it more efficient by simplifying it, which is rationalising it.

clue.text: 13 swears regularly behind setter's back

indicators.note: the regular letters come after the other piece
turned back, so those letters are reversed

parts.note: the setter's is short for the setter is, I'M

indicators.note: taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A stingy person keeps cursing behind the setter's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is MEANIE. 'regularly' takes SER from 'swears'; 'back' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending it, which makes him a meanie.

clue.text: Nothing in Lancashire town demolished

indicators.note: a demolished building is knocked down, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: No trace is left of a Lancashire town knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England, where the dialect word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowt is northern English dialect for nothing, so it is what nothing is called in Lancashire.

clue.text: Very unhealthy, like large country houses

parts.note: ill means unwell
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Grand rural mansions are said to be terribly sickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa can be a large house in its own grounds, especially in the countryside.

clue.text: Remain fair, but refuse to pay penalty

parts.note: to keep money is to refuse to pay it over
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: Someone stays decent yet won't pay a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain fair' is weather talk; the wordplay reads keep a fine literally, not handing the penalty over.
explanation.definitionFit: When weather keeps fine it stays dry and bright, which is remaining fair.

clue.text: Give a hand to catch bull

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them, to clap
to trap is to catch

explanation.surface: Applaud someone for capturing a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' looks like the animal but is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, which is what bull means as slang.

clue.text: Metal content of cage?

definitions.meaning: the middle of the word cage is AG, the chemical symbol for this metal

explanation.surface: A query about what metal a cage is made from.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the middle letters of 'cage', AG, which is the chemical symbol for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.
